rationale: Both responses get the central idea right: alert on progress, through token-emission rate or heartbeat, rather than absolute duration. Both add phase awareness, SLO burn rates and a page-versus-ticket split. B is more rigorous in classifying stalls. It distinguishes a frozen heartbeat with an idle GPU (kernel hang) from a frozen heartbeat with a busy GPU (a stuck verification loop or graph replay). A's quorum requires low GPU occupancy and so would miss that second case. B separates a backpressure stall at the memory cap (ticket) from a hang (page), and treats a low acceptance rate as distribution shift rather than a per-request alarm. It ties T_stall to a multiple of ITL p99 instead of a fixed constant, and it gives standard multi-window burn-rate parameters, where A's windows are muddled. B also adds practical instrumentation guidance: warnings about per-token metric cardinality, full trace capture triggered when the heartbeat fires, scheduler-level KV accounting rather than nvidia-smi, and headroom-based memory alerts. A's per-step signals and phase-suppression rules are good, but B's design is more discriminating and more operationally sound.
